open_points.subject: surface error mapping for stop_required
open_points.text: "`module:surface` returns it unchanged except `internal_error` and `stop_required`, which it answers as `internal_error`." + "`internal_error` | nothing was changed; no detail" + "`stop_required` ... returned up the call chain after the caller wrote its record"
open_points.question: When an operation returns stop_required, should the MCP response still be internal_error even though state may already have changed, or must stop_required have a distinct external code/meaning?
options: Map stop_required to internal_error and accept that internal_error may include committed writes
Expose a distinct stop_required surface code
Keep internal_error but redefine its meaning to allow prior writes in stop-required paths
open_points.default_guess: Map stop_required to internal_error and treat it as a special case that may include prior committed writes.

open_points.subject: Refusal side effects in runs.capture_failed_execution path
open_points.text: "A refusal writes nothing." + "Files `runs` copied into the content-addressed area before `functions.add_captured_trial_case` refused stay there"
open_points.question: If capture_failed_execution ultimately refuses (e.g., functions check fails), are bytes copied earlier allowed to remain, or must the whole operation be side-effect free on refusal?
options: Allow copied bytes to remain even when the operation returns refused
Require rollback/removal of copied bytes so refusal is fully side-effect free
open_points.default_guess: Allow copied bytes to remain, as explicitly described in State 3.

open_points.subject: Approval selection after not_applied resolution
open_points.text: "Which of several approvals with the same `request_digest` ... the oldest `approved` unused one in store order." + "A fresh approval after `not_applied` is one requested after that resolution; approvals recorded before it never count."
open_points.question: When choosing among matching approved-unused approvals, must approvals created before the most recent not_applied resolution for that element be excluded first?
options: Filter to approvals requested after the latest not_applied resolution, then pick oldest in store order
Pick oldest approved-unused matching digest regardless of not_applied history
open_points.default_guess: Exclude pre-resolution approvals, then pick the oldest remaining approved-unused one.

open_points.subject: store.read_records relation: latest activation before a time
open_points.text: "latest activation of a flow version recorded before a time"
open_points.question: Is "before a time" strict (<), inclusive (<=), or actually intended to be determined by store order position relative to run creation?
options: Use store-order position (latest activation record before run-start record) regardless of timestamp equality
open_points.default_guess: Use store-order position before the run-start record to avoid timestamp-tie ambiguity.

open_points.subject: service_invoker.prepare_request redundant service identity input
open_points.text: Inputs: "A ManifestOperation M10 with instance facts, the service identity..."
open_points.question: If the explicit service identity argument disagrees with ManifestOperation.service_id, which one is authoritative and is mismatch refused?
options: Ignore separate service identity and trust ManifestOperation.service_id
Ignore ManifestOperation.service_id and trust separate service identity

open_points.subject: store.remove_run_spool behavior when spool directory is already absent
open_points.text: "Remove the spool of a run the caller names." / Outputs: "Done." / Errors: "`internal_error` on an I/O failure."
open_points.question: If the named run exists but its spool directory is already missing, should remove_run_spool succeed idempotently or return internal_error?
options: Treat missing spool directory as success (idempotent remove)
Treat missing spool directory as internal_error
open_points.default_guess: Treat missing spool directory as success (idempotent remove).
